background.title: Slow structures, fast degrees of freedom, and the morphology of chess openings
background.abstract: Chess openings naturally separate into slow and fast degrees of freedom: pawns evolve through irreversible moves, whereas pieces can be rapidly reorganized within the resulting structure. We exploit this separation to construct a quantitative morphology of opening space. From a catalogue of 3810 named variations, 1749 reach a common depth of $N=10$ plies, corresponding to 619 distinct positions and only 435 joint pawn structures. We characterize these positions through observables measuring pawn commitment and spatial organization, blockade and tension, and piece activity and centralization. Their partial independence reveals a multidimensional opening space and in order to explore its structural organization, we construct a network whose nodes are distinct White pawn structures, connected when a single pawn move or capture transforms one into another. Remarkably, 139 of the 149 observed structures belong to a single connected component containing $98\%$ of all positions. This network exhibits a statistically significant modular organization, with eight communities whose representative structures correspond to familiar pawn formations. Rather than forming isolated categories, these formations emerge as distinct regions of a connected structural landscape. Our approach thus complements the traditional opening taxonomy by revealing similarities between differently named openings and providing a quantitative basis for comparing the positions they produce.

background.title: Liouville transforms for ordinary differential equations with distributional coefficients
background.abstract: We study Liouville transforms for the differential equation $Ju'+qu=wf$ on the real interval $(a,b)$ where $J$ is a constant, invertible, skew-hermitian matrix and $q$ and $w$ are matrices whose entries are distributions of order $0$ with $q$ Hermitian and $w$ non-negative. In particular, we examine their use in the treatment of quasi-regular endpoints and their impact on the Weyl-Titchmarsh $\mathbb M$-function associated with the differential equation.

background.title: The Complex Magnetic Anatomy of a White Dwarf Chromosphere
background.abstract: This study presents phase-resolved spectroscopy and spectropolarimetry of the DAHe white dwarf LP 705-64. Here, two apparently discrete chromospheric regions are observed to alternate in visibility and magnetic polarity with rotation, with field strengths of 9.5 and 22 MG based on the measured Zeeman splitting in Hα. As in the class prototype GD 356, emission line equivalent widths vary in antiphase with the broadband light curve. The 9.5 MG field is visible for 60 per cent of the stellar rotation and stays nearly constant, whereas the 22 MG field increases modestly during the remaining phases. Notably, the time-series transitions between magnetic regions are abrupt and transit-like in morphology, requiring at least one magnetic region to be highly localised and significantly smaller than the areas inferred for the dark surface spots. Both the intensity and the Stokes V/I spectra indicate a field configuration significantly more complex than an offset dipole, but higher-cadence data are necessary to distinguish between a global field and localised magnetic regions. All data are consistent with magnetic, chromospheric, and dark surface regions that are co-located and thus physically related. These findings support a model of chromospheric emission that is intrinsic and localised, consistent with predictions of dynamo-driven electrical currents that heat the upper atmosphere near magnetic poles.

background.title: 5d $\mathbb{Z}_2$ S-folds and Seiberg--Witten curves
background.abstract: We compute the Seiberg--Witten curves for $\mathbb{Z}_2$ S-folds of five-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ rank-1 superconformal field theories. Two complementary constructions are presented. First, we implement the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ action by identifying pairs of points on the original curve, thereby mapping them to a single point on the S-folded curve. Second, motivated by arXiv:2112.14550, we tune mass parameters to special values, corresponding to the insertion of $D_4$ 7-branes. As a nontrivial consistency check, we show that the two Seiberg--Witten curves agree with each other when expressed in the Weierstrass normal form.

background.title: Scarce or Missed Opportunities? Structural Peers and Latin America's Diversification Frontier
background.abstract: Latin America's limited export upgrading is often attributed to failures to seize available diversification opportunities. We distinguish two possibilities: countries failed to realize opportunities demonstrated by structurally similar economies, or upgrading-oriented options were scarce within this peer-revealed set. Using export data for 105 countries from 1962 to 2024, we construct country-specific opportunity sets with an imitation-density measure associated with subsequent product entry. Latin America's deficit arose mainly from scarce upgrading-oriented candidates rather than weak aggregate conversion. Conversion rates matched the global benchmark, but regional frontiers contained few manufacturing products and almost no higher-complexity manufacturing candidates and, unlike East and Southeast Asia, did not shift toward them over time. An illustrative decomposition associates most of the regional upgrading-entry gap with candidate availability. The findings imply that industrial policy should expand feasible upgrading pathways rather than focus only on converting existing opportunities.

background.title: Mode interaction in inclined-layer convection: a physical interpretation
background.abstract: We carry out a numerical investigation of the Oberbeck--Boussinesq equations in a fluid layer inclined against gravity. Equilibria containing different numbers of co-rotating rolls are computed. Mixed-mode branches connect branches containing states with four and six identical co-rotating rolls. These branches display two contrasting routes to reducing (or increasing) the number of rolls, one in which rolls disappear (or appear) and another route in which rolls merge (or split). These results are interpreted in light of the $(2,3)$ mode interaction scenario.

background.title: New Neutron Polarizabilities from Deuterium Compton Scattering at HI$γ$S
background.abstract: Elastic and inelastic Compton-scattering cross sections of the deuteron were measured at HI$γ$S using a circularly polarized, quasi-monoenergetic $γ$-ray beam (61.0 MeV). Scattered $γ$ rays from a liquid deuterium target were detected at $55^\circ$, $115^\circ$, and $150^\circ$. High-resolution NaI(Tl) detectors at backward angles enabled separation of elastic and inelastic events. A $χ$EFT analysis of the data yields new neutron scalar polarizabilities, $α^n_{E1} = 12.25 \pm 1.1\mathrm{(stat)} \pm 0.3\mathrm{(BSR)} \pm 0.8\mathrm{(th)}$ and $β^n_{M1} = 2.95 \mp 1.1\mathrm{(stat)} \mp 0.3\mathrm{(BSR)} \mp 0.8\mathrm{(th)}$ (in units of $10^{-4} \mathrm{fm}^3$) reducing statistical uncertainties by 12 %.

background.title: The BCC lattice is the optimal 3D lattice quantizer for all $p\geq1$
background.abstract: For every finite $p\ge1$, the body-centered cubic lattice uniquely minimizes the $p$th moment of the Voronoi cell among three-dimensional lattices of covolume one, up to orthogonal transformations. This proves the Graf--Luschgy conjecture for three-dimensional lattice quantizers (\cite{GL}).

background.title: SN 2026ahvu in NGC 1433 May Be a Prompt Type Ia Supernova with a Delay Time Under 100 Myr
background.abstract: SN 2026ahvu is a Type Ia supernova (SN) that occurred in the nearby galaxy NGC 1433. Using archival Hubble and JWST imaging from the PHANGS survey, we show that the SN lies within 0.19$''$ and 0.26$''$ of two UV-bright star clusters. This $0.19/0.26''$ separation corresponds to $8/11$ pc ($17/24$ pc) at the reported distances of $9.1$ and $18.9$ Mpc, respectively. The probability of finding an unrelated Type Ia SN this close to a cataloged star cluster by chance is only $\sim$0.4 %. Thus, SN 2026ahvu is likely the first Type Ia SN that can be associated with relatively young star clusters in a nearby galaxy. From spectral energy distribution fitting using HST+JWST (or HST-only) data, we find that the clusters have age estimates of $37_{-5}^{+3}$ ($57_{-9}^{+14}$) Myr and $95_{-13}^{+15}$ ($88_{-12}^{+14}$) Myr. Association with either cluster would mean that SN 2026ahvu should be considered a prompt SN Ia and provide one of the most concrete measurements to date of a prompt Ia delay time. The median age of the younger star cluster is close to the minimum possible delay time for SN Ia progenitors. If the SN is indeed associated with the younger cluster, it would imply that Type Ia SNe can occur almost immediately after white dwarf formation. If the SN is associated with the older cluster, this discovery still presents the first example of a prompt Type Ia SN with delay time under 100 Myr.

background.title: The Gibbons--Penrose inequality in Minkowski spacetime
background.abstract: We prove the Gibbons--Penrose inequality for smooth closed spacelike codimension-two submanifolds of Minkowski spacetime whose past null second fundamental form is non-negative. The proof is motivated by the Alexandrov--Bakelman--Pucci technique.

background.title: Resolving non-neutrality across scales in a hyperdiverse tropical forest
background.abstract: Different ecological processes operate at different spatial and temporal scales. Macroscopic regularities can therefore be captured by descriptions that ignore microscopic details, even when those details are mechanistically relevant to ecological processes. Here, we develop a framework inspired by statistical mechanics to track interspecific spatial correlations under spatial coarse-graining. To do so we combine random-matrix filtering with a spatially explicit neutral model. Applying this approach to eight censuses of the Barro Colorado Island tropical forest, we observe a continuous crossover from an interacting to an effectively neutral organization. Below a few tens of metres (20--35~m), the empirical correlation spectrum differs from neutral expectations, revealing scale-dependent species-specific structure. Part of this structure can be attributed to environmental heterogeneity. However, residual spatial associations provide candidate signatures of biotic interactions or other unmeasured ecological, non-neutral processes. With increasing spatial coarse-graining, empirical and neutral correlation spectra progressively converge, and above the crossover scale the neutral model provides an accurate description of the measured collective organization. Neutrality thus emerges as an effective description of the collective organization of the forest above a characteristic scale, without implying that species are equivalent at the individual level. Our framework provides an operational way to locate that scale.

background.title: Constructing Casimirs for the quantum reflection equation
background.abstract: We explore the quantum reflection equation in the case of a full-dimensional $n\times n$ matrix $\mathbb A$. Using the technique of $q$-determinants, we find closed expressions for the quantum Pfaffian (in the case of even $n$) and for new quantum Casimirs that are ratios of special quantum (Sklyanin) minors of $\mathbb A$. Special attention is paid to the self-adjointness property of the newly constructed Casimirs. We put forward a conjecture that, adopting a natural ansatz for a quantum deformation of a Casimir of a classical algebra, self-adjointness implies commutativity. We also explore the relationship to networks of quantum cluster variables.

background.title: Type IIB Forms and Scalars from an $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ Topological Field Theory with Boundary
background.abstract: We formulate the scalar and form-field sector of type IIB supergravity as an eleven-dimensional topological field theory with boundary. Unlike the pseudo-action, it is a genuine action principle with manifest global $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ symmetry. The IIB fields arise as edge modes: a boundary term breaks the $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ gauge symmetry to $\mathrm{SO}(2)$, so the axion-dilaton parametrizes $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SO}(2)$, and the boundary field equations give the duality relations, including $F_5$ self-duality. As the action never refers to the axion-dilaton directly, S-duality monodromies become holonomies of a flat connection.

background.title: Elastic Wave Imaging via Kirchhoff Migration: Resolution Analysis and Inclusion Identification
background.abstract: We consider the inverse problem of determining the location, orientation, shape, and material parameters of a small elastic inclusion embedded in a homogeneous medium from full-aperture measurements of the scattered field. Using a small-volume expansion, we derive explicit leading-order expressions for four Kirchhoff migration imaging functionals, denoted by PP, PS, SP, and SS, corresponding to the four combinations of pressure (P) and shear (S) waves used for receiver- and source-side backpropagation. The resulting point-spread functions quantitatively characterize the resolution of each mode and show that the SS mode achieves the highest spatial resolution. For an elliptic inclusion, we show that the PP mode uniquely determines the elastic moment tensor (EMT) within the leading-order asymptotic model, thereby enabling the reconstruction of the material and geometric parameters of the inclusion. For a general small scatterer, the reconstruction may instead be interpreted as an effective elliptic representation determined by its leading-order EMT. For a disk, the parameter-identification problem is underdetermined; nevertheless, explicit upper and lower bounds on its volume are derived. We further analyze the model error arising from neglected cross-mode contributions when the distance from the center of the measurement configuration is not sufficiently large relative to the elastic wavelengths. Numerical experiments support the theoretical predictions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed imaging and reconstruction methods.

background.title: On Superconformal Index Degenerations and Half-Indices in S-Confining Gauge Theories
background.abstract: We study the $p \rightarrow 0$ limit of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal indices and its relation to half-indices of three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ theories. At the level of special functions, this limit reduces elliptic hypergeometric integrals to basic hypergeometric integrals. The scaling of the flavor fugacities determines the Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions of the chiral multiplets. The gauge multiplet has Neumann boundary conditions. We apply this prescription to s-confining theories with gauge groups $SU(2)$, $USp(2N)$, $G_2$, and $SU(N)$, and recover the half-index identities of several boundary confining dualities, expressed through the Nassrallah-Rahman and Gustafson integrals. For $SU(N)$ with a rank-two antisymmetric chiral, four fundamentals and $N$ antifundamentals, we obtain an analytic proof of the half-index identities proposed by Okazaki and Smith for all $N \geq 5$.

background.title: Fermionic Kaluza-Klein Reductions
background.abstract: We work out the Kaluza--Klein (KK) compactification on a general product spacetime for free spin-1/2 and spin-3/2 fields in arbitrary dimension. The analysis is performed at the level of the action, and the resulting lower-dimensional theory describes infinite towers of massive particles whose masses are related to the eigenvalues of the Dirac and Rarita--Schwinger operators on the internal space. A Hodge-like decomposition is used to write down a KK ansatz for spin-3/2 fields, and the fate of gauge invariance is discussed.

background.title: Online and Survey Representations of Well-Being: Coherence and Cross-Source Correspondence
background.abstract: Digital traces may complement population surveys in the measurement of well-being, but the two sources do not necessarily capture identical constructs. We compare the Human Flourishing Geographic Index (HFGI) with World Values Survey and European Social Survey measures across three domains using structural equation models. The results show strong within-source coherence and construct-specific cross-source correspondence. Cross-source convergence varies across domains; the observed pattern is consistent with stronger correspondence where the underlying indicators are more closely aligned conceptually. Near-perfect agreement would be unexpected, since surveys elicit standardized self-reports, whereas HFGI captures naturally occurring public expressions. HFGI should therefore be viewed as a distinct but empirically connected measurement system that complements survey-based evidence on well-being.

background.title: Erratum to: Monotonicity of Ursell functions in the Ising model
background.abstract: In this note, we correct an error in the proof Theorem 1 of Comm. Math. Phys. 401 (2023), 2459-2482.

background.title: Non-asymptotic First- and Second-Order Tail Brackets for the Kostlan-Shub-Smale Field and Spherical k-Spin Complexity
background.abstract: For the Kostlan-Shub-Smale field $X$ of degree $k\ge3$ on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, we prove the two-sided bound $(1-\varepsilon(u))\,δ_{*}(u)\le\mathbb{P}\{\sup X>u\}\leδ_{*}(u)$ at every finite $(k,d)$, where $δ_{*}(u)$ is the expected number of critical points above $u$, halved when $k$ is even, and $\varepsilon(u)$ is explicit for $ρu\ge\min\{d-1,\frac32\sqrt{2(d-1)}\}$. The gap is therefore at most of order $e^{-(1+ρ^{2})u^{2}/2}$ with $ρ^{2}=k/(2(k-1))$. We also give $δ_{*}$ itself in closed form, as a finite sum of Hermite polynomials, together with a two-term envelope that is asymptotically sharp and a single-monomial relaxation of the form $Cu^{d-2}e^{-u^{2}/2}$. As an application we bracket the annealed complexity of the spherical $k$-spin Hamiltonian at every finite $(k,d)$: the upper bound holds at every energy, a lower bound of the same form at every energy above $9/4$ times the spectral edge $\sqrt{2(d-1)}/ρ$, above twice the edge when $d\ge10$, and is consistent with the Auffinger-Ben Arous-Černý complexity function as $d\to\infty$.

background.title: The enigma of locally Toeplitz matrices. I. Discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential
background.abstract: Freezing the coefficients of a banded locally Toeplitz matrix gives a family of Toeplitz eigenvalue measures. Their average can fill a region of the complex plane even when the eigenvalues of the original matrices appear to follow curves. We conjecture that, when the above average has a sufficiently regular planar density, the limiting eigenvalue measure is its mother body. We prove it for a class of finite Dirichlet discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential $V$ and a common real coefficient $α>0$ on the two adjacent diagonals. When $(\Im V)'>0$ and $V$ admits a suitable holomorphic extension, the limiting measure is supported on finitely many analytic arcs. Its logarithmic potential falls below that of the averaged measure by twice the least of four explicit actions. We obtain these actions from a four-term asymptotic expansion of the Dirichlet determinant. When $\Im V$ is not monotone, an exact transfer recursion gives a conditional extension. For a circular potential arc we verify the geometric switching condition, leaving non-resonance as the remaining hypothesis.

background.title: Regime change in a model for political opinion dynamics
background.abstract: Political crises involving a series of violent events are the rule rather than the exception in history. Here, we use a minimal opinion dynamics model to describe regime change as a contested transition between dominant shared ideas in a society. New opinions spread with a cumulative advantage, and agents do not return to opinions they held before, resulting in recurrent boom-and-bust dynamics without tuned parameters. During a transition, opinion changes grow approximately exponentially and then saturate in the finite system, declining approximately linearly as spreading is limited by the shrinking interfaces between opinion groups. We compare qualitative features of these transitions with historical data of political violence, used as an empirical proxy for contested transitions. A permutation test shows that violent events cluster in time in the dense Chinese and US records. Around their peaks, violent events rise in an accelerating way and then decline; in the Chinese data, the decline is consistent with the approximately linear decline in the model. We also use a fragmentation measure that serves as an early warning signal for transitions in the model. Overall, the patterns in the empirical data and the dynamical behavior of the model could contribute to a better understanding of long-term historical processes.

background.title: Dynamic signatures of collective knowledge through navigation in a network with semantic structure
background.abstract: What distinguishes how humans navigate an information network like Wikipedia from what the underlying graph structure and language statistics alone predict? To study human collective navigation, we analyze 70,770 human trajectories through Wikispeedia, an online game where players navigate between articles to reach a target. To compare groups of trajectories rather than individual ones, we merge all trajectories leaving or entering a given article into a Flow Tree. Flow Trees compress collections of trajectories into hierarchies of group splits. We build forward and reverse Flow Trees for 815 of the most commonly traversed articles, representing divergence and convergence, respectively. We compare humans against four random-walker null models, either unweighted or weighted by graph structure, word frequency, or semantic similarity to target. Human Flow Trees are deeper with longer trunks and later splits, indicating players stay together longer than random walkers, whose Flow Trees tend to fan out immediately. An article's degree predicts 51.3-70.9% of the variation in Flow Tree branching factor for random walkers, but only 24.1-36.2% for humans. Taking what graph structure fails to predict as a two-dimensional coordinate system, we define four article types (beacons, funnels, forks, and corridors), distinguished by how humans enter and exit them. These human-defined types are not explained by out-degree or title-word frequency are, and are not recovered by any random walker. A fifth null model, built from first-order human click preferences, partially reproduces human Flow Tree shape but differs significantly in how much of that shape degree explains. We consider collective knowledge to be the structure shared by players who never communicate, beyond what graph structure imposes. It comprises first-order click preferences and a significant component that extends across clicks.

background.title: Perfect Wave Transfer in Nonconformal Tomonaga-Luttinger Liquids
background.abstract: Perfect wave transfer (PWT) reproduces spatial reflection at a common finite time under a fixed Hamiltonian. We classify this process for open compact bosons and inhomogeneous Tomonaga--Luttinger liquids, distinguishing transfer of oscillator and neutral observables from transfer on the charged field algebra. In the single-charge model, the first two notions coincide. Global transfer additionally requires rephasing of the compact zero mode. For regular reflection-symmetric channels, exact oscillator transfer forces an odd multiple of the optical crossing time and a strictly ordered, parity-compatible spectrum differing from the conformal ladder at only finitely many levels. This spectral condition is also sufficient when the Robin boundary data induced by the physical profile are included. Requiring Neumann conditions after the Liouville transformation instead forces conformality. We construct an explicit, regular one-defect family for every $r>1/2$. Its transfer parameters are precisely the reduced fractions $r=p/q$ with odd numerator and denominator, with shortest transfer time $pL/v_0$. At the delay $3L/v_0$, the $r=3/5$ profile has numerical contrast $K_{\max}/K_{\min}\simeq 12.913$, compared with $81$ for $r=3$. Two independent conservative discretizations show second-order convergence on fixed mode bands. Occupation- and charge-constrained error estimates quantify robustness, while an exact homogeneous-chain calculation explains the $J^{2/3}$ resolved-band scale also observed in the engineered channels. These results provide a spectral design method and finite-device benchmarks for quadratic quantum channels. An interacting microscopic realization remains open.

background.title: Incentive Pathologies in a Live LLM Agent Arena: An Empirical Study of Concentration, Reward-Rule Implementation Discrepancy, and Network Dilution
background.abstract: We audit one live LLM agent arena (AITRAP; 22 autonomous agent seats, ~96,000 reasoning nodes) over nine days (Oct 16-25, 2026), during which the platform deployed two bundled incentive changes: a progressive tax reform (V2.9.3, Oct 19) and a seed-inversion with explorer-side action update (V3.0, Oct 21). These serve as before-and-after markers, not cleanly isolated interventions. Four exploratory predictions are tested against ten data frames (F1-F10) using the Gini coefficient, Top-K concentration share, code-level reconstruction of the continuation-bonus mechanism, and the Mann-Kendall trend test. The Gini analysis is inconclusive at 95% confidence (bootstrap intervals straddle 0.7). The Top-4 node-activity-score share falls from 97.2% (Oct 19, pre-V2.9.3) to 49.4% (Oct 25, post-V3.0; 56.7% under a merge-seat assumption). The continuation bonus, announced as depth-based x10, resolves at code level to a four-condition anti-abuse gate paying x2.85 in the typical case and permanently blocking the self-continuation it superficially rewards; the gate was active ~40 hours before the V3.0 announcement. The events-per-node ratio declines significantly (Mann-Kendall S=-45, z=-3.94, p=8.3e-5) from 7.36 to 7.069. We discuss implications for incentive designers, the announcement-implementation gap, and public peer review as an event record.

background.title: Finite-strain second-gradient elasticity with an energetic surface: existence of minimizers, incremental theory and elastocapillary beading
background.abstract: We develop a finite-strain theory of second-gradient elasticity for solids with a material surface endowed with its own constitutive energy. The bulk second gradient plays two complementary roles. First, under suitable coercivity assumptions and convexity with respect to the second gradient, we prove the existence of minimizers for nonnegative, lower semicontinuous surface energy densities, without requiring convexity, polyconvexity, positive one-homogeneity, or an upper growth bound on the surface energy. Second, it introduces an intrinsic bulk length scale that affects the onset of instability and wavelength selection. To investigate these effects, we derive an incremental small-on-large formulation in the finitely deformed configuration and apply it to the elastocapillary beading of an axially stretched soft cylinder. For an infinite cylinder and the parameters considered, increasing the second-gradient modulus delays bifurcation and shifts the critical mode towards longer wavelengths. Above a finite threshold of this modulus, the critical stretch saturates in the long-wave limit. The model is implemented in the open-source finite element code OOFEM using C1-continuous isogeometric analysis. Finite-cylinder simulations yield onset stretches in close agreement with the analytical predictions. Selected post-bifurcation branches traced by arc-length continuation exhibit beaded states and supercritical bifurcation at small second-gradient moduli, whereas larger moduli are associated with subcritical bifurcation and the formation of distinct thick and thin segments.

background.title: Remark on residual solutions in the $KBc$ algebra
background.abstract: In this paper we study residual solutions of open bosonic string field theory in the $KBc$ algebra with the auxiliary identities $(\partial^mc)^2=0$ of the ghost field. These solutions are not covered by the classification based on the defining relations alone. We show that the operator which controls the cohomology on the residual family depends only on $s=γ_1+γ_2$. At positive level $n$, cohomology can appear only on the lines $s=\pm n$. We compute it through level four and find one class at every point of each line $s=-3$ and $s=-4$. These classes give exact polynomial deformations of the residual family. At level six on $s=-6$, the cohomology instead vanishes generically and has dimension two at $(-1,-5)$ and $(-5,-1)$. We also compute the failure of the standard generator redefinition to preserve the auxiliary identities, and discuss the regularization of an explicit residual solution.

background.title: A Jump-Diffusion Model of Home Price Dynamics and Neighborhood Change
background.abstract: We develop a dynamical model that links the fluctuations of individual home prices to changes in the full distribution of home prices in an urban area. We model the price of an individual home as a jump-diffusion stochastic differential equation. To capture the dynamic and hyper-local economic conditions that drive the residential real estate market, we allow all parameters to depend on both time and neighborhood. In the mean-field limit, we derive the associated Fokker-Planck partial integro-differential equation (PIDE) governing the evolution of the home price distribution in a neighborhood. We quantify spatial heterogeneity within a city by using the Wasserstein-2 distance to compare home price distributions across the city's neighborhoods. We validate our model using data from Boston, Massachusetts as a case study.

background.title: Predicting next-week VIIRS fire detections in Bolivia: a reproducible benchmark with temporal and geographic evaluation
background.abstract: Weekly detection forecasts could help prioritize fire monitoring across Bolivia. We estimate the probability of at least one fire detection by the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) on the Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership satellite in each 0.05-degree cell during the following 7 days. Primary models were fixed before test scoring. Calibrated LightGBM, a gradient-boosted decision-tree model, reaches 2023-2025 temporal-test average precision (AP) of 0.323 (95% block-bootstrap interval 0.222-0.383), compared with 0.167 for climatology and 0.143 for persistence. Its paired AP gain over climatology is 0.1567 (0.0998-0.2179). A separately selected geographic model reaches AP 0.384 versus 0.181 for persistence in regions excluded from fitting. In the temporal-test population, reviewing the highest-ranked 5% and 10% of eligible area would have covered 38.4% and 55.8% of cell-weeks with detections. Probabilities still overestimate detection frequency in the highest-probability group. Retrospective rainfall provides no clear AP improvement; the primary validation comparisons for vegetation, land cover and their combination are inconclusive. Positive secondary or exploratory intervals do not change those decisions. Evaluation requires complete target and recent-history observations and measures satellite detections, not individual fires, causes or burned area. Prospective evaluation should archive inputs at each weekly issue and measure ranking, calibration and the usefulness of selected cells for monitoring decisions.

background.title: The dynamics through the first two Lagrange necks in the small-mass restricted three-body problem
background.abstract: We study the planar circular restricted three-body problem (PCR3BP) for sufficiently small mass ratios, from low energies to slightly above the second Lagrange value. We show that retrograde orbits around the primaries and Lyapunov orbits at the necks form the binding of a finite energy foliation. We construct these foliations using the theory of pseudoholomorphic curves in symplectizations developed by Hofer, Wysocki and Zehnder. Slightly above the second Lagrange value, the dynamics is transverse to families of disks bounded by the retrograde orbits, and cylinders connecting the retrograde orbits to the Lyapunov orbits, forming a $3-2-3-2$ foliation. The proof uses the rotating Kepler problem and Hill's lunar problem to control the singular limit as the mass ratio $μ\to 0$. As a consequence of the foliation, both Lyapunov orbits have infinitely many homoclinic orbits.

background.title: On the Volume Conjectures for Dehn-filled $3$-manifolds along fundamental shadow link complements with big volume
background.abstract: We prove the Volume Conjecture and the Asymptotic Expansion Conjecture for closed oriented hyperbolic $3$-manifolds obtained by integral Dehn-fillings along a fundamental shadow link complement, provided that their volumes are sufficiently close to that of the complement. More generally, we show that the conjectured asymptotic expansions hold for pairs obtained by change-of-pair operations on a fundamental shadow link complement whenever the volume of the corresponding hyperbolic cone manifold is sufficiently close to that of the complement. A key ingredient in the proof is the introduction of extended quantum $6j$-symbols and a Weak Reflection Symmetry satisfied by them. The Weak Reflection Symmetry is established by relating the extended quantum $6j$-symbols to the $b$-$6j$ symbols through a real Gevrey-$1$ estimate and a truncated Borel-Laplace transform.

background.title: The Localization Scale of the Block Anderson Model in One Dimension at Arbitrary Coupling and Volume
background.abstract: We study the one-dimensional block Anderson model with independent $W\times W$ Gaussian unitary ensemble potentials and deterministic nearest-neighbor hopping, with hopping-to-disorder ratio $g$. The system consists of $L$ blocks, with total dimension $N=WL$. As $W\to\infty$, we identify the bulk localization length, up to an arbitrarily small power of $W$, with $\min\{N,\max\{W,W^2g^2\}\}$, uniformly for deterministic couplings $g\ge0$ and cycle lengths $L\ge3$. For every fixed $D>0$ and all sufficiently large $W$, the expected fraction of eigenvectors in the selected energy interval satisfying these bounds is at least $1-W^{-D}$. In polynomial volume the bounds hold simultaneously for all eigenvectors in that interval with probability at least $1-W^{-D}$. The localization length is the number of coordinates in the shortest cyclic interval containing at least half of an eigenvector's mass.

background.title: Induction instead of Feynman diagrams, L-functionals instead of Hilbert space
background.abstract: The main result of this paper is a construction of an inductive process that can replace Feynman diagrams. Combining this result with the notion of the L-functional, one can give an exposition of QED that does not suffer from infrared divergences

background.title: Zak Phase, Pole--Zero Invariants and the Maslov Index of Bloch Cauchy Lines in One-Dimensional Periodic Media
background.abstract: The topological properties of the Bloch bands of a one-dimensional periodic medium are described either by the Berry--Zak phase or by the poles and zeros of the surface impedance. We show that both can be read from one geometric object: the line spanned by the field and its flux (the Cauchy data) at an inversion centre. For each band, this line turns as the quasi-momentum runs over the Brillouin zone. Its number of turns, the Maslov index, is fixed by the parities (even or odd) of the Bloch functions at the two band edges, and its parity is the Zak phase. In a gap, the Cauchy line of the solution decaying on one side rotates monotonically with the energy, and an interface state between two crystals is a crossing of two such lines. This gives the known criterion of at most one state per gap in terms of the same lines. Examples with a stratified medium show that the choice of inversion centre changes the interface spectrum. The last section discusses what is missing to extend the construction to higher dimension.
